title: Only one H1 is allowed

spec.name: llms.txt (llmstxt.org)
spec.normative_quote: An H1 with the name of the project or site. This is the only required section
spec.note: The spec describes exactly one H1; a second H1 is a local structural convention we enforce, not a spec-tested conformance failure -- conformance_testable is false. Verified against the pinned source (AnswerDotAI/llms-txt @c7178b9, nbs/index.qmd) on 2026-07-30: the quote is exact (Format list item 2). Source line 42 has no trailing period; a stray one was removed in this review pass.

policy_note: llmstxt.org never states a prohibition on a second H1 -- 'this is the only required section' means the H1 is the only mandatory element, not that no other H1-level heading may appear. The prohibition this rule enforces is entirely our own inference (required does not imply exclusive); the source text contains no such rule. rule_class stays convention / conformance_testable stays false, which is the intended, correctly-modeled outcome.
applicability: An llms.txt body that already has a valid H1.
expectation: No further line matches /^#\s+\S/. Emission is PER OFFENDING LINE, not once per body: a body with three H1s emits this finding twice. Stated explicitly because the ADR 0036 Posture-3 rehearsal produced a blind regeneration that emitted once, passed every case then declared, and diverged from the implementation on 113 of 20,000 fuzz inputs -- the multiset assertion is count-sensitive, so only a case with TWO extra H1s can discriminate the two readings (cases/two-extra-h1s.txt below).

cases.name: two extra H1s emit the finding twice (ADR 0036: pins per-line emission, which no single-violation case can discriminate)
a second H1 appears after the first
